description: Staff+ engineer level (Principal, Staff, Distinguished, 8+ years experience). Evaluates org-wide technical strategy, multi-year architecture roadmaps, build vs. buy evaluations, organizational Conway's law alignment, and executive influence.

axes.depth: Holistic domain mastery: distributed systems economics, global platform governance, compliance, enterprise resilience, and organizational dynamics.
axes.ambiguity: Extreme ambiguity; problems involve vague, conflicting company priorities, emerging technologies, or multi-year structural transformations.
axes.expectedScope: Organization-wide or multi-team platforms, cross-company technical strategy, foundational architecture bets, and engineering culture.
axes.followUpPressure: Strategic pushback on long-term maintainability, talent constraints, opportunity cost, vendor lock-in, and organizational headwinds.
axes.behavioralExpectations: Unifying technical vision, navigating organizational politics gracefully, sponsoring underrepresented talent, and driving cultural change.

relevance.name: Relevance & Directness
relevance.description: Aligns engineering strategy with overarching business viability, financial runway, and organizational leverage.

anchors.1: Advocates for ivory-tower architecture disconnected from business reality, budget constraints, or team capabilities.
anchors.3: Directly links architectural strategy to business ROI, engineering leverage, and organizational sustainability.
anchors.5: Masterful strategic synthesis: re-frames the problem around competitive advantages, capital efficiency, and sustainable velocity.

structure.name: Structural Framing
structure.description: Employs macro-level architectural frameworks: business capabilities -> domain boundaries -> platform primitives -> migration vectors.

anchors.1: Lacks cohesive strategic vision; jumps between disparate micro-level tactics without establishing guiding principles.
anchors.3: Comprehensive strategic framework: clearly sets guiding principles, domain boundaries, phased migration phases, and governance.
anchors.5: Visionary structure: articulates clear decision matrices, risk mitigation milestones, and cultural change roadmaps effortlessly.

depth.name: Technical & Conceptual Depth
depth.description: Evaluates foundational tech choices across decades: data sovereignty, zero-trust security, multi-cloud economics, and legacy modernization.

anchors.1: Out-of-touch with modern technical realities or relies on dogmatic patterns that no longer match industry state of the art.
anchors.3: Deep and broad mastery: understands cross-platform primitives, cost modeling, data mesh concepts, and resilience patterns.
anchors.5: Profound insight: evaluates ecosystem trends, hardware/cloud cost curves, kernel/compiler evolutions, and org-level leverage points.

clarity.name: Clarity & Articulation
clarity.description: Communicates seamlessly with VP/C-suite executives, cross-functional leads, and junior engineers alike.

anchors.1: Overly condescending, impenetrable jargon-heavy monologue, or inability to tailor communication to different audiences.
anchors.3: Speaks with empathy, clarity, and authority; builds consensus through compelling arguments and rigorous active listening.
anchors.5: Inspirational communicator: simplifies profound complexities into irresistible narratives that drive swift organizational alignment.

levelFit.name: Level Alignment
levelFit.description: Calibrated against Staff/Principal engineer expectations of company-wide leverage, culture building, and multiplying others.

anchors.1: Functions merely as a senior individual contributor solving isolated tickets without company-wide leverage or impact.
anchors.3: Authentic Staff engineer: multiplies whole engineering teams, sets architectural standards, and leads high-risk strategic initiatives.
anchors.5: Distinguished caliber: reshapes company-wide engineering culture, foresees multi-year industry disruptions, and builds durable platforms.
